title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 193 (Agent’s responsibility for sub-agent appointed without authority)

content.overview: Section 193 provides that where an agent, without having authority to do so, has appointed a person to act as a sub-agent, the agent stands towards such person in the relation of a principal to an agent, and is responsible for his acts both to the principal and to third persons; the principal is not represented by or responsible for the acts of the person so employed, nor is that person responsible to the principal.
content.glance: Where an agent appoints a sub-agent without authority, the agent is a principal to that person and is responsible for his acts to both the principal and third persons. The principal is not represented by or responsible for that person, and that person is not responsible to the principal.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Where an agent, without having authority to do so, has appointed a person to act as a sub-agent, the agent stands towards such person in the relation of a principal to an agent, and is responsible for his acts both to the principal and to third persons; the principal is not represented by or responsible for the acts of the person so employed, nor is that person responsible to the principal.

examples.title: Unauthorised sub-agent
examples.body: Agent appoints a sub-agent without authority. Agent is responsible for that person’s acts to both principal and third persons; principal is not bound by or responsible for that person under Section 193.

hypotheticals.question: Agent appoints a sub-agent without authority. Is the principal bound by the sub-agent’s acts?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Under Section 193 the principal is not represented by or responsible for the acts of the person so employed. The agent is responsible for those acts both to the principal and to third persons.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 193
